result:
`pricebook.py` had 11 rules whose behavior didn't match their docstrings. I fixed all of them, taking the docstrings (and the shared rules in the module docstring) as correct.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 11 | A "whole" rule computed its discount marginally (only units above the threshold) | Discount on the full amount |
| 12 | The 30,000 cap only applied once the discount went over 60,000 | Cap always applies |
| 20 | The cap was applied to the price, not the discount | Cap applies to the discount |
| 56, 70 | Same price-capping problem, in "marginal" rules | Cap applies to the discount |
| 96, 128 | "Marginal" rules computed their discount on the full amount | Discount only on units above the threshold |
| 107 | Rate was 3% instead of 2% | 2% |
| 120, 136 | Rate was 6% instead of 5% | 5% |
| 150 | A "whole" rule computed its discount marginally | Discount on the full amount |

I also changed rule 101 from `qty > 12` to `qty >= 12` to match the docstring. Its results don't change, because a marginal discount at exactly the threshold is 0 anyway.

To check, I wrote a script outside the repo that reads each docstring's type, rate, threshold and cap and builds the expected result from them. It compares all 150 rules over quantities 0 to 129 plus 200, 500 and 1000, against eight unit prices. Before the fixes those 11 rules mismatched; after, none do. I didn't run the repo's own tests, if it has any.

STATUS: DONE
